F2 S293's quoted span is 221-223 (sentence starts on 221, ends on 223); the landed cell cites line 221 and counts 17 tokens including the ellipsis. Both spans stay under the 25-word cap.

F3 The frozen plan names re.html for S294 and rejects it; the working-tree registry instead rejects the GnuPG handbook as S294. The L1's own l1/pre-append-url-check.txt shows the duplicate-URL check that encountered S143 (re) and S263 (hashlib) before the landing.

F4 re.html cannot become a new row: its URL is S143's, and the round-75 lesson withdrew S283 for the same page and scope ('ids are not reused, so S283 stays a gap'). The frozen plan's sentence at plans/round-78-claims.md:132-133 is therefore a screening record unless the L1 moves the GnuPG row to S295 before committing.
F5 The re.html snapshot is currently deleted from the working tree (uncommitted), while it remains committed at HEAD; the plan-named source has bytes only in git right now.
F6 The GnuPG row's used-by cell is '-' whereas S291 (the round-77 rejected row) uses '—'; cosmetic inconsistency for a rejected row.
F7 The GnuPG anchor cell states 12 words; the quoted string has 11. Both are under the 25-word cap, so the quote is valid; the count is off by one.

F8 used-by for S292/S293 points at two untracked knowledge entries; if the landing commit omits them the registry cells dangle. Both files exist in the working tree and cite the rows at their first line.
